   Longer-term health risks of haze need greater attention
 The impact of air pollution on individuals and public health burden may be more wide-ranging.

 Short-term exposure to high PM2.5 levels can irritate the eyes and airways, causing coughing and breathing difficulties.

 Seow Wei JIe
 Published   Nov 04, 2026, 05:00 PM

 Set as preferred source Unlock audio 中文 The thick, choking smoke that blanketed large parts of South-east Asia since August appears to have dissipated in Singapore in recent days, with the arrival of rain and a shifting of the winds.
 While we can breathe a bit easier and put away the N95 masks for the moment, questions remain: What damage does the haze do to our health, particularly if it recurs every year?
